hook_text: Colour the world by climate and it looks like the planet is wearing stripes.
clip_script: At the equator, a green stripe of rainforest: the Amazon, the Congo, Indonesia. On each side, savanna, with grass and scattered trees. Then, near the tropics, the deserts line up: the Sahara in the north, the Kalahari and Namib in the south. Next come Mediterranean and subtropical stripes, then temperate and continental, then tundra and ice at the poles. But the stripes bend. Cold currents push deserts right onto west coasts. Warm currents make east coasts humid. Mountains make cool islands even at the equator. Zoom into South Africa and you see it all in one country: desert in the west, Mediterranean Cape Town, humid KwaZulu-Natal, snowy Lesotho, and rain falling from east to west.
visual_style: A whiteboard globe being coloured in stripes, then bent by blue and red current arrows, then a zoom into a colour-coded map of South Africa with an arrow showing rain decreasing westward.
pacing: Smooth zoom out, a pause on the stripes, then a fast zoom in.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and colour your own climate map.
